_meta.description: Structures / formulas of CLASSIC perfumes and reference-book accords for the Perfumista knowledge base. Each entry captures the compositional skeleton, the note pyramid, olfactory character (smells_like), and how the combination defines its genre (what_it_does).
_meta.critical_caveat: Perfume houses NEVER publish real bench formulas. For almost all branded classics only the STRUCTURE / accord is public; 'parts' is therefore null unless the source is a genuinely published book formula (Askinson, Poucher, Aftel) or a working perfumer's per-1000 skeleton. Where numeric percentages appear for a brand (e.g. Chanel No.5, No.19), they come from Calkin & Jellinek's published ANALYSIS/reconstruction, NOT the manufacturer. Note pyramids sourced from Fragrantica/marketing are flagged as such in the ingredient notes and are distinct from the real structural materials. NEVER treat marketing note lists as a formula.

confidence_scale.documented: Real published formula/analysis with parts, OR a single-material composition. Sources: Askinson (public domain), Poucher, Aftel, Calkin & Jellinek analysis, published perfumer skeletons.
confidence_scale.partial: Structure and key materials well documented (often with a published reconstruction or a generic accord's percentages), but the brand's own ratios are not public. parts usually null; any numbers are from reconstruction/analysis, not the maker.
confidence_scale.structure_only: Only the accord/material skeleton is public; no proportions exist. Pyramid may be marketing-derived. parts = null.

sources: Calkin & Jellinek, Perfumery: Practice and Principles (Wiley, 1994) - published ANALYSES of Chanel No.5, No.19, Arpege, mellis/oriental accords
Poucher, Perfumes Cosmetics and Soaps Vol. II (fougere no.1017; Solid Amber)
Askinson, Perfumes and Cosmetics (1892, public domain via Project Gutenberg #55735) - real cologne formulas with parts
Mandy Aftel, Essence & Alchemy (amber accord parts)
Ohloff, Pickenhagen & Kraft, Scent & Chemistry (2nd ed. 2022) - Azzaro PH percentages
Octavian Coifan / 1000 Perfumes - Cool Water reconstruction
The Good Scents Company (material data, CAS verification)
Basenotes community reconstructions (Aventus, L'Heure Bleue) - flagged hobbyist
nstperfume.com, perfumeshrine, boisdejasmin, cafleurebon, monsieurguerlain (historical reviews/analyses)
Fragrantica / brand copy (note PYRAMIDS ONLY, flagged as marketing)
_meta.language_note: Research conducted in English per source availability; field values kept in English to match source terminology.

formulas.name: Coty Chypre

ingredients.note: Top; bright citrus that opens the accord and creates the chiaroscuro contrast against the dark mossy base
Base; the defining material of the family - inky, earthy, woody-green; provides the mossy-animalic foundation and fixation
Base; warm resinous ambery-leathery depth; the third pillar (raw material historically associated with Cyprus/'Chypre')
Base; earthy woody reinforcement of the mossy foundation
Heart; luminous floral core lifting the dark base
Heart; softens and rounds the floral center
Base; animalic warmth and diffusion (period fixatives)

formulas.smells_like: Dry, mossy-green and resinous, with a sparkling citrus opening dissolving into an earthy, bitter, leathery-ambery forest-floor depth. Austere, sophisticated, chic rather than sweet.
formulas.what_it_does: Codifies the chypre genre by pairing a bright, volatile bergamot top directly against a dark, low-volatility oakmoss + labdanum base - the tension between fresh citrus and damp mossy resin IS the chypre effect. Oakmoss supplies bitter-green inky earthiness, labdanum supplies warm ambery-leathery sweetness, and bergamot lights the whole structure; the floral heart bridges them. CAVEAT: no genuine published numeric formula for Coty Chypre exists publicly - STRUCTURE only. Pyramid detail leans on descriptive accounts; all proportions unknown.

formulas.name: Guerlain Mitsouko

ingredients.material: Gamma-undecalactone (aldehyde C-14 / peach lactone; via Firmenich 'Persicol' base)
ingredients.note: Heart; signature velvety, fleshy ripe-peach-skin note layered over the chypre base - the innovation that created the fruity chypre. Not truly an aldehyde but a lactone; Persicol base marketed by Firmenich from 1908
Top; citrus opening of the underlying Coty-style chypre accord
Base; the austere, bitter mossy backbone that the peach lactone tempers into velvet
Base; resinous ambery depth of the chypre foundation
Base; earthy-woody support
Base; dry rooty woodiness
Heart; floral volume
Heart; floral rounding
Heart/base; warm spicy accents (cinnamaldehyde ~104-55-2, clove/eugenol ~97-53-0)

formulas.smells_like: A dry, mossy, autumnal chypre wrapped in a soft, fleshy, slightly sour ripe-peach warmth - the fruit reads as skin/velvet rather than juice, sitting over a bitter-green, spicy, ambery-woody base. Melancholic and refined.
formulas.what_it_does: Takes the austere Coty-Chypre skeleton (bergamot / oakmoss / labdanum) and layers a lactonic peach note (gamma-undecalactone, 'aldehyde C-14') into the heart. The peach lactone's creamy, fatty, fruity character plushes up and tempers the sharp bitterness of the oakmoss, creating a velvety bridge between citrus top and mossy base - this defines the fruity-chypre sub-genre. CAVEAT: material roles and the Persicol/aldehyde-C14 story documented; numeric formula NOT public. Pyramid note names largely marketing-derived (Fragrantica).

formulas.name: Guerlain Shalimar

ingredients.note: Top; unusually large citrus overdose (reportedly ~30%+ in hobbyist reconstructions, NOT official) giving the bright, almost fresh opening contrasting the vanilla base
Base; the key innovation - a more powerful, creamier vanilla molecule than vanillin, added to the Jicky-type base for the ambery-gourmand drydown
Base; classic vanilla; Jacques Guerlain reportedly used an impure grade (guaiacol/phenol traces) giving smoky darkness
Base; hay-like powdery sweetness - part of the Jicky/guerlinade core; with vanilla creates the powdery warm-skin effect
Base; balsamic resinous warmth - vanillin+coumarin+opoponax+labdanum forms the basic Shalimar accord
Base; sweet balsamic vanillic resin, part of the amber-vanilla core
Base; resinous ambery 'deep shadows' of the oriental drydown
Base; almond-powdery softening layer
Base; warm balsamic-vanillic fixative
Heart; powdery elegance
Heart; softens the base (guerlinade floral part)
Heart; brings light/volume (guerlinade floral part)
Base; animalic warmth and diffusion

formulas.smells_like: A bright, almost citrus-cologne opening that melts into a vast, creamy, smoky-powdery vanilla-amber - leathery, animalic and balsamic, with a custardy sweetness cut by resins and incense. Warm, plush, lipstick-powdery.
formulas.what_it_does: Builds on the Jicky base (lavender + vanillin + coumarin) and the guerlinade signature, then overdoses ethyl vanillin and bergamot to push it into amber-oriental. Genre effect comes from extreme contrast: a huge fresh bergamot top over an enormous creamy vanilla-coumarin-opoponax-benzoin-labdanum base - vanillin/coumarin give powdery warm-skin diffusion, ethyl vanillin the gourmand creaminess, resins/animalics the smoky depth. This citrus-over-vanilla-amber template essentially defines the modern oriental. CAVEAT: PROPORTIONS NOT officially published; figures online (bergamot ~30%+) are hobbyist reconstructions - all parts null.

formulas.smells_like: A dense, dry, herbal-aromatic chypre: bitter chamomile tea and sage over a huge earthy patchouli-oakmoss body, with a rosy floral core. Booming, tailored, no sweetness - often read as woolly, medicinal, almost incense-like.
formulas.what_it_does: A chypre (bergamot/floral/oakmoss) re-centered on a massive patchouli accord held in contrast against airy hedione and cooled by herbal chamomile/sage/coriander. That contrast - heavy earthy patchouli vs transparent jasmonate - is why it reads as both crushing and luminous, and it re-drew the classic French chypre for an American department-store audience (lineage shared with Cabochard, Aramis). CAVEAT: structure_only. No published quantitative formula exists; the repeated ~20% patchouli is a blog estimate. Pyramid marketing-derived.

Simultaneously cold/melancholic and warm/comforting - like violet-scented pastry and face powder.
formulas.what_it_does: Defines the powdery semi-oriental by pairing an unusual anisic-aldehyde top with heliotropin's almond-vanilla powder, then floating soft white florals over the guerlinade base (vanillin + coumarin + tonka + iris + benzoin). The anise/heliotrope tension produces its bittersweet cold-yet-cozy twilight character; the guerlinade gives Guerlain family DNA. CAVEAT: source_url is a hobbyist GCMS-informed reconstruction ATTEMPT, NOT Guerlain's proprietary ratios; parts null. Pyramid marketing-derived.

formulas.smells_like: A warm, plush fruity chypre: a jammy, boozy prune-and-peach heart draped over mossy, resinous, faintly animalic depths. The modern version adds a dirty, warm-skin cumin funk; the vintage is more lemon/aldehyde-bright and immortelle-dusty on top.
formulas.what_it_does: Femme created the fruity chypre by marrying a rich stone-fruit accord (Roudnitska's Prunol = heliotropin + gamma-undecalactone + fruity esters) to a classic oakmoss chypre base with an animalic (civet/benzoin) drydown. The lactonic fruit sweetness against dry oakmoss makes the genre voluptuous yet elegant. CAVEAT: NO quantitative formula published (parts null). Load-bearing correction: cumin belongs to the 1989/2013 reformulations, not Roudnitska's 1944 original - the original's funk came from civet/animalics. Pyramid marketing-derived.

formulas.smells_like: A dense, sweet-spicy amber: warm clove and cinnamon over a thick benzoin-balsam-vanilla base with animalic muskiness. Rich, tenacious, almost edible-resinous; famously long-lasting.
formulas.what_it_does: The archetype of the American spicy amber (oriental). Structurally it sits on the 'mellis' accord (salicylates + eugenol/clove + patchouli + hydroxycitronellal + coumarin over balsams) documented by Calkin & Jellinek, wrapped in a heavy benzoin/labdanum/vanilla amber base. Salicylates give lift/skin-diffusion while balsams and vanilla give sweetness and enormous tenacity, so the spice reads warm and enveloping - the template later reworked by Opium and Coco. CAVEAT: the mellis percentages describe the GENERIC accord, NOT Youth Dew's proprietary formula; pyramid is marketing (Fragrantica). Parts null.

formulas.name: Houbigant Fougere Royale

ingredients.note: Real structural role: bright herbal-medicinal top/heart giving the accord its freshness; one of the three defining pillars. Original ratio not published.

ingredients.material: Tonka bean / clary sage / spices (rondeletia accord)
ingredients.note: Marketing note list from Houbigant/Fragrantica for the modern reconstruction; original 1882 formula not public, only the archetypal skeleton documented.

formulas.smells_like: Fresh aromatic lavender opening over a soft, hay-sweet coumarinic warmth grounded in earthy-green oakmoss - clean, herbal, powdery, the original 'barbershop' effect.
formulas.what_it_does: Defines the fougere genre itself: fougere accord = lavender (fresh herbal top) + coumarin (sweet hay/tonka warmth) + oakmoss (earthy mossy base), with bergamot lift and geranium in the heart. The three pillars create structural clarity - fresh at top, warm in middle, grounded at base. Coumarin's 1882 use made it the first fragrance built on an aroma-chemical, launching modern synthetic perfumery and every later fougere.

formulas.what_it_does: Jicky defines the fougere (and prefigures the oriental) by pairing a natural lavender/citrus/herb top with the then-new synthetics linalool, coumarin and vanillin, laced with animalic civet. The lavender-coumarin-vanillin trio is the structural backbone every later fougere quotes; using multiple synthetics abstractly (rather than imitating one flower) is why it is called the first 'modern' perfume. formulas.smells_like: A cool, soapy, sparkling 'champagne' fizz of aldehydes bursting over a creamy abstract floral bouquet (jasmine-rose-ylang-iris), settling into a warm powdery sandalwood-musk-vanilla drydown. Famously 'not a flower' but the abstraction of many.
formulas.what_it_does: Defines the floral aldehydic genre: an overdose of aliphatic aldehydes C-10/C-11/C-12 (~1% total - huge for 1921) laid over a rich natural rose-jasmine-ylang-iris bouquet. The aldehydes add a fatty, waxy, citrus-soapy diffusive 'lift' and abstraction that detaches the scent from any single flower, while methyl ionone + ylang + hydroxycitronellal build the floral body and coumarin/vanillin/musks give the warm base. That aldehyde-over-bouquet accord is the template copied by Arpege, Madame Rochas, Rive Gauche, White Linen. NOTE: percentages are Calkin & Jellinek's published analysis, not Chanel's formula.

formulas.smells_like: Close cousin of No.5 but warmer, rounder and more floral-honeyed - a soft aldehydic shimmer over a dense rose-jasmine-ylang bouquet with a peachy nuance, drying to a woody (vetiver), animalic, lightly vanillic base. Less soapy/sharp than No.5.
formulas.what_it_does: Arpege takes the No.5 aldehydic-floral template and evolves it: the aldehyde top is gentler, the floral heart elaborated through compounded floral bases, the woody/vetiver and animalic notes pushed up, and - critically - vanillin and coumarin dialed back. Calkin & Jellinek identify this vanillin/coumarin reduction as the pivot that opened the way to drier, mossier later masterpieces (Caleche, Madame Rochas, Calandre, Rive Gauche). CAVEAT: descriptions from published analysis; no standalone ratios, parts null.

formulas.what_it_does: The textbook fougere skeleton descended from Fougere Royale (1882). Its defining trick is the lavender-coumarin-oakmoss triad: aromatic lift of lavender/bergamot, sweet hay warmth of coumarin, green mossy earthiness of oakmoss form a self-contained three-point structure. No single fern smells like this - it is an abstract 'idea' accord, which is why it became the template for virtually all masculine perfumery. Poucher's no.1017 fleshes the triad out with florals, woods and animalic/musk fixatives for body and tenacity. NOTE: genuine published book formula with real parts (per 1000).

Widely credited as one of the first men's-marketed fragrances. CAVEAT: 61% lavender is a Caron marketing claim; other notes marketing-derived; no verified 1934 ratios, parts null.

Firmenich's Olivier Cresp built the whole family on this maltol+patchouli axis. Schoen's conceptual point is that one well-chosen material can be a finished, genre-launching fragrance, birthing the whole molecular-perfume category.

ingredients.note: REAL published parts from Mandy Aftel, 'Essence & Alchemy'. Sweet vanillic-balsamic bulk of the accord.
REAL published parts (Aftel). The ambrein-rich resinous, faintly leathery/animalic backbone that defines 'amber'.

ingredients.dilution: neat; if using crystalline vanillin, CAS 121-33-5, dose ~10% solution
ingredients.note: REAL published parts (Aftel). Rounds and sweetens. Vanillin (121-33-5) is the common synthetic substitute.

formulas.smells_like: Rich, dark and sticky-sweet - like dark toffee or caramel warmed by resin, not quite edible because of a faint leathery whisper from the labdanum.
formulas.what_it_does: This three-material triangle IS the classic 'amber' (never real amber/ambergris - a fantasy accord). Labdanum supplies warm animalic-resinous depth, benzoin sweet balsamic body, vanillin rounded sweetness; together they form the oriental heart of countless fragrances (Shalimar, Ambre Antique, Obsession). Poucher's textbook 'Solid Amber' uses the same skeleton scaled up (Labdanum/Vanillin/Benzoin core), confirming labdanum+benzoin+vanillin as the genre's defining structure. NOTE: parts are a genuine published book formula.

formulas.smells_like: A luminous, slightly fruity jasmine tea - radiant and airy from the Hedione, sweet-fruity from benzyl acetate, with a whisper of narcotic 'dirty' indole and a soft musky-balsamic drydown.
formulas.what_it_does: Defines the white-floral genre by reconstructing natural jasmine from its molecular parts: benzyl acetate + jasmine absolute give the recognizable body, Hedione (huge dose, ~38%) supplies the transparent radiance that made post-1970s florals feel modern and diffusive (its debut in Eau Sauvage/No.19 changed perfumery), and trace indolic materials add the living, slightly carnal edge that separates a real white floral from a candy floral. Musks and benzyl benzoate fix and extend it. NOTE: genuine working perfumer's formula with real per-1000 parts - not marketing.
